intent: The key cap showing the letter or number the root's shortcuts mode assigned to a QuestionnaireChoice.
typical_uses: The key hint a QuestionnaireChoice renders at the end of its row

dont_use_when.situation: Showing a keyboard key in running text or a menu

invariants.text: The cap is aria-hidden always, and carries the native `hidden` attribute and no `data-shortcut` while the root assigned its choice no shortcut (no `shortcuts` mode, a disabled choice, a choice missing from its item's `choices` in `items`, or more choices than letters or digits).
QuestionnaireChoice renders one QuestionnaireChoiceShortcut itself and is the only provider of the context this part needs, so a consumer-placed one is always a second cap in the row.

anti_patterns.dont: Nest a QuestionnaireChoiceShortcut in a QuestionnaireChoice's children
anti_patterns.do_instead: Rely on the cap the choice renders; set the key assignment with the root's `shortcuts`

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the cap's own state (`QuestionnaireChoiceShortcutState`: shortcut), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.

good.title: Letter shortcuts assigned from the root

bad.title: A hand-written cap in the children
bad.why: The row already renders its own cap, and a hand-written letter does not bind the key; only the root's `shortcuts` mode does.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireChoiceShortcutState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies. The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the cap's own state (`QuestionnaireChoiceShortcutState`: shortcut), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted.
